entries.clue: Becomes too much for captain after wicket in cricketing stints (10)

indicators.note: HELM comes after W, so W goes first
W and HELM sit inside OVERS

blocks.note: an over is a bowler's spell of six balls in cricket
W is the scorecard abbreviation for a wicket
to captain is to helm, to steer

annotation.surface: A cricket captain is worn down by long spells in the field after taking a wicket.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket words all serve the wordplay: an over is a set of six balls bowled by one player, and W marks a wicket in the scorebook.
annotation.definitionFit: To overwhelm someone is to become too much for them.

entries.clue: Cockneys live in these units? (4)

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their H, so this is how a Cockney says the word

blocks.note: homes, with the Cockney dropped H

annotation.surface: A question about where Londoners of the East End make their homes.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners, famous for dropping the H, so 'homes' comes out as 'omes. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, so ohms are units in the physicist's sense.

entries.clue: Oriental net assets regularly disappearing (4)

definitions.note: Oriental is an adjective; EAST works as one in 'the east wing'

indicators.note: every other letter goes, at regular intervals

blocks.note: nEt AsSeTs: the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters stay

annotation.surface: A business report about an Eastern company whose net assets are steadily vanishing.
annotation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd-placed letters of NETASSETS leaves E, A, S, T.
annotation.definitionFit: Oriental comes from the Latin for rising, as the sun does in the east, so it is a plain synonym for eastern.

entries.clue: I beg your pardon!? 'Down with the solver', etc? (4,4,3)

blocks.note: 'What?' is the blunt way of asking someone to repeat themselves
to down a drink is to have it
the person solving the crossword is you

annotation.surface: An outraged exclamation at a slogan calling for the crossword solver's downfall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down with' looks like a protest cry; here 'down' is the verb to drink. 'What have you' is the casual equivalent of etc at the end of a list.
annotation.definitionFit: 'And what have you' ends a list the way etc does.

entries.clue: Swift in air (7)

blocks.note: an adjective: fast, as a train or a delivery can be
a verb: to air a view is to voice it

annotation.surface: A swift, the bird, darting through the sky.
annotation.walkthrough: Swift reads as the bird and air as the sky it flies through; instead swift is the adjective and air is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Express means fast, and to air an opinion is to express it.

entries.clue: Some acclaim and elation for country's first democratic leader (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

blocks.note: acclaiM AND ELAtion

annotation.surface: Cheers and joy greet a nation's first democratically elected leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first president chosen in a fully democratic election in 1994, and the surface fits the celebrations that followed.
annotation.definitionFit: Mandela was the first president of democratic South Africa.

entries.clue: Kindly reject bitterly cold Frenchman (4)

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: M is short for Monsieur
raw weather is bitterly cold

annotation.surface: A polite request to turn away a chilly Frenchman.
annotation.walkthrough: M + RAW makes MRAW, which read backwards is WARM, the opposite of the cold in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Warm used of a person means friendly and affectionate, a plain synonym for kindly as an adjective.

entries.clue: Booze, a kiss and music in retreat in old city (10)

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so AIR is reversed

blocks.note: ale is beer
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
used as it stands
an air is a tune

annotation.surface: Drink, romance and music on a getaway in an ancient city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' sounds like a holiday; it turns AIR backwards. 'And' is not a joining word here but three letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Alexandria is an ancient city in Egypt, founded by Alexander the Great.

entries.clue: Cleans up: as does autumnal gardener? (5,1,4)

blocks.note: to clean up is to make a lot of money
a gardener in autumn rakes the fallen leaves into a pile

annotation.surface: A gardener tidying the fallen leaves in autumn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleans up' looks like tidying, which the gardener really does; in the first sense it means making a fortune, as does making a pile.
annotation.definitionFit: To make a pile is to make a lot of money, as when someone cleans up.

entries.clue: Mild and soft cheese a Roman partakes of no end, primarily? (10)

indicators.note: take each word's primary, that is first, letter

blocks.clueFragment: Mild and soft cheese a Roman partakes of no end
blocks.note: Mild And Soft Cheese A Roman Partakes Of No End

annotation.surface: A Roman who eats endlessly of a mild, soft cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is also the start of the wordplay: the first letters of every word before 'primarily' spell the cheese, so the clue describes itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is an Italian cream cheese, famously used in tiramisu, both mild in taste and soft in texture.

entries.clue: Kiss with audacity (4)

blocks.note: to kiss and cuddle, informally
British slang for nerve or cheek

annotation.surface: Kissing someone boldly.
annotation.walkthrough: In British English 'neck' means cheek or nerve, as in 'what a neck!', as well as kissing.
annotation.definitionFit: Necking is kissing, and neck is British slang for audacity.

entries.clue: Sweet-chasers consumed snacks (6,6)

indicators.note: what is consumed is broken down, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: People after sweets gobbling up some snacks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet-chasers' tempts you to think of cheese, the course that follows the sweet, but the hyphenated phrase is just the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheese straws are thin savoury pastry sticks served as snacks.

entries.clue: A little drunk makes suggestive gesture, being game (11)

blocks.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
a wink is a suggestive signal

annotation.surface: A tipsy person winking flirtatiously, apparently up for anything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game' reads as willing, as in 'game for it'; it is the definition, the noun. Tiddlywinks is flicking small counters into a cup.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a game played with small discs.

entries.clue: Like, stressed (10)

blocks.note: the surface makes it a teenage filler word; the setter means similar to, in the manner of
the surface means anxious; here the word points at itself, printed in italic type, which is how print shows stress

annotation.surface: A teenager's verbal tic before admitting they feel under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: The word 'stressed' is set in italic type in the printed clue; so the clue means 'like the word stressed', which is italicised, and italic type is itself used to stress words.
annotation.definitionFit: Italicised words are printed in slanting type, often to stress them.

entries.clue: Qualities of estates? (10)

blocks.note: the characteristics a thing has
pieces of land and buildings owned

annotation.surface: An estate agent's question about what makes a house worth having.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the qualities of properties are also properties.
annotation.definitionFit: Properties are both qualities and pieces of real estate.

entries.clue: Overhits, lacking at first – after training, does well (7)

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter
training reshapes, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: OVERHITS without its O

annotation.surface: A tennis player who overhits early on but, after practice, plays well.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits the surface in two sporting moments; in the wordplay, 'after training' is the instruction to rearrange what is left of OVERHITS.
annotation.definitionFit: Thriving is flourishing, and a plant, business or child that flourishes is doing well: a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Worked out the bill, perhaps made sense (5,2)

blocks.note: totalled the figures
an explanation that adds up makes sense

annotation.surface: Checking a restaurant bill and finding it was right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' tells you the bill is just one example of something added up.
annotation.definitionFit: Added up means both totalled and made sense.

entries.clue: Impudence: slip audibly giving you mouth (3-4)

indicators.note: what is heard, not what is spelt: say SINK and write SYNC

blocks.note: lip is cheek, backchat
to slip down is to sink

annotation.surface: Cheek from someone who lets slip a mouthful of insults.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' reads as insolence to go with impudence; it is the verb, to mouth the words without singing them, which is what lip-syncing is.
annotation.definitionFit: To lip-sync is to mouth words along to a recording.

entries.clue: Bread in such a pâtisserie (7)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: suCH A PÂTIsserie, ignoring the accent

annotation.surface: Bread sold in a smart French pastry shop.
annotation.walkthrough: A chapati is an unleavened Indian flatbread, the last thing a pâtisserie would stock.
annotation.definitionFit: Unleavened Indian flatbread, cooked on a griddle, so a bread by broad category.

entries.clue: Everyman is going to ... is going to ... show spite (3,4)

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I'll, with the apostrophe dropped
will = is going to

annotation.surface: The setter, stammering with rage, trying to announce a spiteful act.
annotation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so 'Everyman is going to' is 'I will', shortened to I'LL. The stutter of the surface is the second helping.
annotation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility that wishes someone harm, which is what spite amounts to: a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Visible wisdom (2,5)

blocks.note: two words: within view, able to be seen
one word: deep understanding

annotation.surface: Wisdom that shows itself.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration (2,5) fits the first meaning; the second runs the words together as INSIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: In sight means visible; insight means wisdom.

entries.clue: Notice – noticed – small tools (8,4)

blocks.note: a circular is a notice sent round
saw = noticed
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

annotation.surface: A notice about some little tools that someone has spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small' seems to describe the tools, but circular saws are big; it only supplies the S.
annotation.definitionFit: Circular saws are power tools with a round blade.

entries.clue: And, finally, Vienna roll comes round (4)

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the next three words

blocks.note: viennA rolL comeS
O is round in shape

annotation.surface: A closing news item about a Viennese bread roll going the rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And, finally' sounds like the last story of a news bulletin, but 'And' is the definition and 'finally' works on the words after it. A Vienna roll is a crusty white bread roll.
annotation.definitionFit: Also and and both add something further.

entries.clue: Tiny shred of memory: morsel, did you say? (4)

indicators.note: the question asks about the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a bite is a morsel of food

annotation.surface: Someone half-remembering a small scrap of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Memory' looks like recollection; here it is a computer's memory, measured in bytes.
annotation.definitionFit: A byte is a small unit of computer memory.

entries.clue: Escape, knocking back lager (4)

indicators.note: knocking back sends the letters backwards

blocks.note: Pils is a pilsner lager

annotation.surface: Someone escaping reality by downing lager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' is drinking in the surface and turning the word round in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dog slips its lead, a prisoner slips his guards, both getting free.

entries.clue: A little bit alarmingly disturbed (10)

indicators.note: disturbed things are moved out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Someone somewhat, and alarmingly, upset.
annotation.walkthrough: The two adverbs seem to contradict each other, a little bit yet alarmingly; the first is the definition and the second the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: From margin, it means by a narrow amount, as in marginally better: a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Money needed when haircut's hard (4)

blocks.note: a do is a hairdo, and the 's adds S
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

annotation.surface: A complaint that you need cash when times are tough for a haircut.
annotation.walkthrough: Dosh is British slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal British slang for money.

entries.clue: The Britons gathered: Ruby, Beryl and 10 more (10)

definitions.note: the definition lists examples, all of them birthstones

indicators.note: gathering pulls things together into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A roll call of Britons, including women named Ruby and Beryl.
annotation.walkthrough: Ruby and Beryl look like old-fashioned British first names; they are gems. There are twelve birthstones, one per month, so these two and ten more.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruby and beryl are among the twelve birthstones, each linked to a month.
